bg-note.note: Blockquote panel only. Too close to the page to carry a transient highlight; selection uses accent-ink instead.

fg-subtle.note: Dark moved from 0.76 to 0.71: at 0.76 it was identical to Muted Ink, so the nested-list and footnote step existed only in light. Now 7.31:1 on the dark page.

accent.note: A fill, never text. Tried as the selection background and measured 4.41:1 against Paper — rejected for accent-ink.

accent-ink.note: Links, footnote refs, focus ring, and the selection background against Paper text: 6.2:1 light, 10.3:1 dark.

accent-code.note: Dark moved from 0.82 to 0.87: at 0.82 it was identical to Ember Ink, so inline code and links were the same colour in dark. Now 11.73:1.

border-strong.note: Light is exactly fg, so rule and label read as one mark. Dark moved from 0.93 (also exactly fg-dark) to 0.76: the two measured near-symmetric (17.66:1 light, 15.28:1 dark) but read asymmetric — a light line on a dark ground blooms, and seven near-white bands were louder than the 11px labels beneath them. At 0.76 the dark rule is 8.73:1 against the page, the weight of secondary text; that also clears WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 for the task-list checkbox outline it draws, which is a component boundary rather than text.

code-comment.note: Darkened from 0.56 to 0.54: the lighter value measured 4.20:1 against Sunken Paper in light and missed AA. At 0.54 it is the system's lowest measured pair, 4.58:1.

display.purpose: The page title, once. The only large type in the system; drops to 2.125rem below 34rem and hyphenates, so a long single-word APP_NAME breaks at a syllable rather than mid-word.

lead.purpose:
The single sentence after the title, clamped to 40ch so it sits on a shorter measure than the body column and registers as an opening rather than as the first paragraph. The clamp moved with the column: at 48ch in the narrowed 34rem column the lead filled 88% of it and no longer read as a shorter measure, while 40ch is 400px — 74% of the column, still three lines. 34ch broke it into four lines that read as a wrapping accident, and below 34rem the clamp is inert, so this is a desktop decision. The selector is h1 + p and stays literal: a plain APP_TEXT_LEAD still renders as one

after the

and gets the treatment, but text opening with a heading or a list correctly gets none.

label.purpose: Section heads (h2) in the sans face, uppercase and tracked, always beneath the 2px rule.

headline.purpose: h3 at 20px — the first heading that reads as a heading rather than a label, and the last level with a size of its own.

title.purpose: h4 at body size in bold Ink.

title-quiet.purpose: h5 (bold) and h6 (medium) at body size in Muted Ink — the two levels that separate by tone and weight because the scale has no size left.

body.purpose: All prose, in a 34rem column with text-wrap: pretty — 75 characters on the first line, counted in the browser over the paragraph's own text nodes, not converted from ch.

label-mono.purpose: Table heads (0.12em) and figure captions (0.08em) — machine-shaped labels, never sentences.

code.purpose: Inline and block code in the self-hosted IBM Plex Mono.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: The only breakpoint: tightens page padding and shrinks the display and lead sizes.

lineWeights.name: rule
lineWeights.purpose: Structural: the section-head rule, the table head underline, the focus outline. Never above a block without an uppercase label.

lineWeights.name: hairline
lineWeights.purpose: Dividers: table rows, hr, nested-quote stripe, the footnote block's top line, unchecked checkbox.

knownLimits.name: Scroll containers carry no tabindex
knownLimits.detail: pre and table scroll without tabindex="0". Chromium makes scrollable regions focusable itself — measured, pre.chroma is a tab stop with a visible ring — but that is browser behaviour, not a guarantee. Markdown cannot set the attribute and the page carries no JavaScript.

knownLimits.name: Footnote reference target size
knownLimits.detail: Footnote references measure 6x12px. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 exempts targets inside a block of text, so this is an ergonomic note rather than a conformance failure.

knownLimits.name: Failed template keeps the 500 status
knownLimits.detail: A broken {{ in the mounted file is answered with the environment-variable page via handle_errors, but the status stays 500 on every path so the operator still sees the failure. The branch guard (eq (placeholder "http.error.status_code") "") is load-bearing: without it the error route re-renders the broken file and returns a zero-byte body.

knownLimits.name: The table's slack all goes to the last column
knownLimits.detail: width: 100% on the last cell is what makes a narrow table reach the column edge, so a table ending in a short value gets a wide final column. Distributing the slack evenly needs table-layout: fixed, which trades away content-driven column sizing and was rejected for that reason.

measure.name: measure
measure.purpose: The page column. Counted in the browser over real text nodes: 75 characters on the first line (82 at 40rem, 63 at 30rem). The comfortable range is 45-75.

measure.name: measure-lead
measure.purpose: The lead sentence. 400px, 74% of the column, three lines — short enough to read as an opening. ch is the width of the digit zero, not a character count; this token is sized by proportion to the column, not by a character claim.

components.name: Placeholder Surface
components.description: The default page: a title and one sentence, vertically centred by min-height rather than height. It carries none of the system's marks — no rule, no uppercase label, no mono, no accent — by decision; a placeholder is allowed to look like almost nothing. APP_TEXT_LEAD runs through the same markdown renderer as a mounted file, so every mark is one markdown line away; only APP_NAME is emitted as a literal h1 and escaped with | html, so a name is never reformatted by its own value and never breaks out of the element it names. This is also the error surface: a failed template re-serves this page rather than a maintenance screen.
components.css: .ds-placeholder { display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; min-height: 20rem; padding: var(--space-14) var(--space-6) var(--space-16); background: var(--bg); color: var(--fg); font-family: var(--font-sans); } .ds-placeholder h1 { margin: 0 0 var(--space-3); font-size: var(--text-xl); font-weight: var(--weight-bold); letter-spacing: var(--tracking-tight); line-height: var(--leading-tight); hyphens: auto; } .ds-placeholder p { margin: 0; max-width: var(--measure-lead); font-size: var(--text-md); line-height: var(--leading-snug); color: var(--fg-muted); }

narrative.overview:
amber looks like a page torn out of a well-set manual: a flat sheet, ruled into sections, with nothing on it that is not text. There is no chrome, no card, no container — the page *is* the container. The system serves two surfaces of very different weight, and both have to look deliberate: a heading and one sentence on an otherwise empty window, or an operator's markdown file rendered whole. One declaration serves both — the column is centred vertically by `min-height` rather than `height`, so two lines sit mid-viewport and a long document grows from the top under the identical stylesheet. Both reach the same element vocabulary, because `APP_TEXT_LEAD` runs through the same markdown renderer as a mounted file. What separates the surfaces is where the text comes from, not what it can be. `APP_NAME` is the one thing held back from the renderer and set as a literal `h1`: composed into the same markdown document it came back as `

star site

` (measured), and a page title must not be reformatted by its own value. The principle runs both ways — `APP_NAME` is emitted through `| html` in `` and `<h1>`, so markup written into a name shows as characters instead of breaking out of the element it names. `APP_TEXT_LEAD` stays unescaped, because markdown there is the promise. There is no build chain and no runtime fetch: the monospace face ships inside the image as two `woff2` files, so the page renders complete with the machine offline.
keyCharacteristics: Flat sheet, no shadows, no radii, no gradients, no motion.
Two line weights only: a 2px structural rule and a 1px hairline.
Uppercase tracked labels for section heads, table heads and captions.
One warm accent; four code tones; everything else neutral at hue 250.
Styled by element selector — the renderer emits no classes to hook.
Light and dark are peers, both measured to AA, with the same tone relations.
One surface only — the failed page is the placeholder page, not an error design.

rules.name: The Four Tones Rule
rules.body: Syntax highlighting has exactly four colours. A new Chroma token class joins one of the four groups in app/style.css or it stays body colour. A fifth tone is not added to distinguish a fifth category.

rules.name: The Measured Palette Rule
rules.body: No colour value ships until its pair has been measured in-browser against the surface it actually sits on, in both schemes. The floor is 4.5:1; 26 of 26 pairs clear it and the lowest is 4.58:1 (code comment on Sunken Paper, light). This rule bit once and is recorded so it bites again: the first selection highlight used {colors.accent} and measured 4.41:1, so the shipped value is {colors.accent-ink} at 6.2:1 light and 10.3:1 dark. A value is never lightened to make a design read better.

rules.name: The Mirrored Scheme Rule
rules.body: Dark is not a separate palette, it is the same *relationships* inverted — which is not the same as the same lightness values. Two tokens once collapsed onto their neighbours in dark only — Subtle Ink onto Muted Ink, Ember Deep onto Ember Ink — silently deleting distinctions the light scheme still made. When a token moves, check its neighbours in the *other* scheme. The heavy rule is the documented exception: mirroring Ink's lightness literally made a line that measured almost identically (17.66:1 light, 15.28:1 dark) read far louder, because a light line on a dark ground blooms and a dark line on a light ground does not. Where perception and arithmetic disagree, perception decides which value ships and the number is measured afterwards to prove it is safe — never the other way round.

rules.name: The One Warm Hue Rule
rules.body: Outside code blocks the page carries a single warm family: the accent and the note tint. A second accent hue is not introduced to mark a new kind of content; tone, rule weight or the mono face does that job.

rules.name: The Ruled Label Rule
rules.body: A section head sits directly beneath a full-width 2px rule. The rule and the label are one unit: neither appears without the other. The heavy rule appears in exactly two places — the section head and the table head — and both carry an uppercase label, which is what makes the rule true rather than aspirational; the footnote block, which the renderer gives no label, takes a hairline instead. Inside one section the eye can meet both, a heavy stripe roughly sixty pixels under another heavy stripe, and it reads as a repeat. That is intended and it is what the rule costs: the fix is never to drop the rule from one of the two places.

rules.name: The Tone-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: The type scale runs out of sizes before markdown runs out of heading levels. h3 is the last level with a size; below it depth steps first in tone (Ink to Muted Ink at h5) and then in weight (700 to 500 at h6), never in size. A future level does the same or does not exist.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Machine Rule
rules.body: The monospace face marks code, table heads and captions. Never body prose, a heading, or emphasis.

rules.name: The Counted Measure Rule
rules.body: A claim about line length is worth what the counting method is worth. ch is the width of the digit zero, not a character count, and in a proportional face it understates the real count — an earlier pass read the column as "74ch" and shipped a line of 82 characters on that reading. The measure is counted in the browser over the paragraph's actual text nodes and held inside 45–75: at 40rem the first line ran 82 characters, at 34rem it runs 75, at 30rem it would run 63. Change the column, count again; never convert.

rules.name: The Unbreakable Column Rule
rules.body: Nothing an operator writes may push the document sideways. Text wraps or breaks; anything with an internal minimum width of its own becomes its own scroll container. A new block picks one of the two mechanisms deliberately, because the body-level wrap rule silently fails to cover the second kind.

rules.name: The Both-Modes Rule
rules.body: Every layout rule is checked against both surfaces — the two-line placeholder and the full markdown page. A rule that only looks right on one of them is not a rule yet.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: Every line is either the 2px structural rule or the 1px hairline. A third weight, a dashed line or a coloured border is not part of the vocabulary.

rules.name: The Tint-Once Rule
rules.body: A tinted surface does not nest inside a tinted surface. A quote inside a quote drops the tint for a hairline stripe; anything deeper does the same rather than stacking washes.

rules.name: The One Surface Rule
rules.body: The system has exactly one error surface, and it is the environment-variable page. No separate error design, no apology copy, no status number set in type, no warning glyph — the failed page *is* the placeholder page. That is the only rendition consistent with never looking like a maintenance screen, and it is why the guard on the branch, not a new template, is where the work went.

rules.name: The Silent Default Rule
rules.body: The default surface carries none of the system's marks — no rule, no uppercase label, no mono face, no accent — and that is settled, not an oversight. A placeholder is allowed to look like almost nothing; the restraint is the statement. Measured: that page loads three files and not one of them is a font. Every mark is available the moment an operator writes markdown into APP_TEXT_LEAD, and nothing is to be added to make the empty state look designed.

dos: Do put every value in app/tokens.css and author it in OKLCH.
Do style by element selector. The renderer emits no classes, so a rule needing a class works for hand-written markup and silently fails on the operator's page.
Do define every colour in both scheme blocks. A token that exists in only one scheme is a bug.
Do hand a control back to the platform (appearance: auto) when forced colours would strip what carries its state.
Do ship any new font file inside the image and declare it with @font-face locally.
Do escape anything an operator sets that is not meant to be markup.
Do delete a token nothing consumes, and restore it the moment something consumes it again. Delete on the evidence of today's build and restore on the same evidence — neither move needs an apology.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow, a border-radius, a gradient, a transition or an animation. The sheet is flat and still.
Don't fetch anything at runtime — no font CDN, no script, no image from another host. The page must render with the machine offline.
Don't dress the default surface up with marks the operator did not ask for.
Don't add a logo, wordmark or decorative image — the product has none by commitment, and the page's only mark is the ruled section label.
